name: rowOrderStats
title: Gets an order statistic for each row in a matrix

origin.description: Gets an order statistic for each row (column) in a matrix.
origin.usage:
rowOrderStats(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, which, dim. = dim(x), ...,
  useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: which
arguments.text: An integer index in [1, K] indicating which order statistic to return.

arguments.name: dim.
arguments.text: An integer vector of length two specifying the dimension of x, also when not a matrix. The argument is named with a period so it does not clash with dim.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: The installed function returns one order statistic per selected row. which is asInteger(which), so TRUE is 1 and a fractional value is truncated toward zero. The selected columns are partially sorted with rPsort or iPsort. Integer x stays integer. A missing value anywhere in x is an error, including a value outside the selected columns. An NA row or column index is an error when the other margin is non-empty.
origin.value: A vector of length N. N is the number of selected rows. The mode is integer when x is integer, and double otherwise.
origin.example:
x <- matrix(1:12, nrow = 4, ncol = 3)
rowOrderStats(x, which = 1)

translation.description: Gets an order statistic for each row in a matrix.
translation.usage: rowOrderStats(x, rows=None, cols=None, which, dim=None, use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 2-d array whose axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. A 1-d vector is accepted when dim is set; it is filled column-major, as R stores a matrix. Integer values stay on the integer path. Floating values are computed as float64. Logical input is rejected. A missing value anywhere in x is an error.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based row subscripts. None selects every row. Zeros are dropped, negatives exclude, and logical values are recycled.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based column subscripts. None selects every column. which is counted on this selection.

arguments.name: which
arguments.text: The 1-based order statistic, after R's asInteger. TRUE is 1. A non-integer double is truncated toward zero. The value must lie in 1 through the number of selected columns.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers giving the number of rows and columns. This is dim. in R. None uses the shape of a 2-d x. A 1-d x is filled in column-major order.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for the R argument useNames. It must be TRUE or FALSE. The result is a plain array, with no names attached.

translation.details: The partial sort lives in the Rust crate roworderstats, ported from matrixStats src/rowOrderStats.c. Each selected row is copied and passed to R's rPsort or iPsort, the same X_PSORT the C template calls. psortKM is not used. The returned value is the element placed at the requested order. Integer input returns int32. A missing value in x, a double NaN included, is an error before the sort.
translation.value: A vector of length N, one order statistic per selected row. Integer input returns int32. Floating input returns float64.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.roworderstats import rowOrderStats

x = np.arange(1, 13).reshape((4, 3), order="F")
rowOrderStats(x, which=1)
